keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 macro nature photo, underground cross-section side view, like looking through the glass side of a soil terrarium. Light brown sandy soil fills the whole frame, with a thin strip of ground surface and short green grass at the very top. A narrow burrow tunnel goes down from the surface and opens into one smooth oval underground chamber in the center of the frame, about half of the frame width wide. On the floor of the chamber lies a cluster of about thirty cricket eggs: each egg is pale cream-yellow, smooth, long oval, about one thirtieth of the frame width long. Soft warm light, sharp focus on the eggs. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the soil, the tunnel, the chamber, the grass, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The eggs are hatching: many tiny newly hatched cricket nymphs crawl out of the eggs on the chamber floor. Each nymph is pale whitish, wingless, with long thin antennae and long hind legs, about one twentieth of the frame width long. Some egg shells are now empty and split open. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the soil, the tunnel, the chamber with the empty split egg shells, the grass, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The group of white nymphs is gone. One small cricket nymph now stands on the chamber floor in front of the empty egg shells, in the center of the frame, seen from the side, head facing left. It is light brown, wingless, with a big round head and long antennae, about one eighth of the frame width long. Only one cricket. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the soil, the tunnel, the chamber, the empty egg shells, the grass, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The nymph in the same place and pose is now much bigger: a plump brown cricket nymph with a large broad head, thick spiny hind legs and small wing buds on its back, about one quarter of the frame width long. Its pale old shed skin lies on the chamber floor just behind it. Only one cricket. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the soil, the tunnel, the chamber, the empty egg shells, the shed skin, the grass, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The large nymph is now an adult female giant burrowing cricket in the same place and pose: plump glossy reddish brown body, very large broad round head, brown wings folded flat over its back, thick spiny hind legs, long antennae, two short tail bristles and a very short ovipositor, about two fifths of the frame width long. A second pale shed skin lies on the chamber floor behind it. Only one cricket. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the soil, the tunnel, the chamber, the old empty egg shells, the shed skins, the grass, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The same adult female cricket, with the same size and colors, stands in the same place with its abdomen bent down to the chamber floor. A new cluster of pale cream-yellow long oval eggs lies on the chamber floor under the tip of its abdomen. Only one cricket. No text, no watermark.
